x: On the 5th stage Eric Gebbett ran steadily but Herne Hill had Jack Heywood and Finchley young Salvatt and our lead was whittled down to 37 seconds.

10 miles in 51m.48secs. by Jack Heywood with Colin then fifth in 58m.6secs. and Wally in 61m.4secs. was to lead to a new English Amateur Native Record for 15 miles in 1hr.17m.25secs. by Heywood who then retired.
Charlie Jones won both sprints in 10.2 and 23.0 and also the high jump with 5'2". Len Orton was well beaten by J. Heywood of Herne Hill in the 3 miles, Len's time being 15m4s.

Ivor Edmonds (Bristol A.C.) was favourite for the title with J.Heywood (H.H.H.) probable runner-up. At 5 miles Dabbs and Edmonds had a clear 44 secs. lead and a mile later were timed at 31.11 (this would have placed Chas. second in the Club 6!).

In those early halcyon days he beat most of his contempories - names like George Knight, Peter Driver, Ken Harland, Eddie Ellis, Jack Heywood and Ian Boyd - and, no doubt, he is tempted at times to think of what might have been.
